title: MCHP: no position. The recovery is real, but the $78.92 target is only 6.4% above spot and the book excludes the name for AVGO overlap
call_reason: Not a buy at the published levels: the allocator gives 0 shares because MCHP is on the book's exclusion list (2026-10-01: it moves too much with AVGO, a holding), and on its own merits the edge is thin, with the $78.92 target 6.4% above the $74.16 close, P(gain) 0.55 and a slightly higher chance of touching the $55 stop (0.51) than the $108.81 take-profit (0.47).
one_liner: Microchip's analog/MCU upcycle is intact: Q1 FY27 sales rose 38% y/y, gross margin is guided flat at 66-67% into December, distributor inventory is a lean 25 days and FY28 consensus EPS is $4.58. At 16.2x that consensus with $5.1B of net debt and the cycle likely maturing near our Oct-2027 horizon, the published target is only $78.92 (research target (12m) $85), so we hold no position. It is also excluded from the book because of its correlation with AVGO.

thesis.point: The earnings recovery is real, and consensus has held since the research date.
thesis.evidence: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) net sales were $1,484.7M (+38.0% y/y) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.76. Q2 FY27 guidance is $1.589-1.618B sales, 66-67% non-GAAP GM and $0.91-0.95 EPS. FY28 (Mar-2028) consensus is $4.58 EPS on $7.43B revenue, unchanged from 2026-09-18 to 2026-10-14.

thesis.point: The near-term cycle does not look overheated: the channel is lean and margin is guided flat.
thesis.evidence: Distributor inventory is 25 days, 'at the lower end' of history (Q1 FY27 call). At Citi TMT (2026-09-09) the CFO said there is no significant stocking or customer inventory build, and management described bookings as the strongest in about four years. GM is guided at 66-67% through FY27 and roughly flat into December, against a 65% GM / 40% operating-margin through-cycle model.

thesis.point: The price already discounts most of this, and the balance sheet caps capital returns.
thesis.evidence: At $74.16 the stock trades at 16.2x FY28 consensus (74.16 / 4.58) and ~18.0x NTM (estimate: 74.16 / (0.5 x 3.65 + 0.5 x 4.58)). Net debt was $5,089M at Jun-2026 (5,361.3 debt - 272.3 cash), or 2.85x adjusted TTM EBITDA. Management keeps the dividend flat (45.5c/qtr, 2.45% yield = 1.82 / 74.16) and plans no buybacks until the balance sheet improves. Upside is +6.4% to the target and +14.6% to the research target (12m), against -25.8% to the $55 thesis break.

variant_view: There is no real variant view versus the Street on direction; our view differs on the multiple, and the Street is well above us. Our weighted set of 22 analyst targets (as of 2026-10-13, from MarketBeat; consensus rating Buy) has a weighted median of $95, a weighted mean of $102.04 and a range of $69-125. That implies 20.7x and 22.3x FY28 consensus (95 / 4.58; 102.04 / 4.58). The S&P Global consensus on StockAnalysis is higher still: 26 analysts, average $107.84, median $108, range $80-135 (2026-10-14). Our forecasters use 18.5-19x NTM, because at the Oct-2027 horizon the market will be pricing FY29 on a mature upcycle, with the 10-yr Treasury at 5.21% (2026-10-13). The options market on its own is less constructive than we are: median $71.93, P(gain) 0.48, 15th percentile $42.98. Our forecasters on their own are more constructive: median $92.56, P(gain) 0.70. The published blend (0.67 market, 0.33 forecasters) gives a $78.92 median and P(gain) 0.55. Our edge over the options market is about 7 points of P(gain) (0.55 vs 0.48) and rests on the lean channel and the flat-GM guide, which is too little to override the book's exclusion.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $85 (supervisor; agents $83-86, mean $84.3) blends three methods. (1) P/E, weight 0.5: 18.75x x ~$4.60 NTM EPS at Sep-2027 = $86.25 (estimate; consensus FY28 $4.58 rolled forward, less a light cycle haircut; 575M non-GAAP diluted shares). (2) FCF yield, weight 0.3, equity basis: ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45 / 0.05 / 0.575; 2.6 / 0.052 / 0.575; FCF ~33% of ~$7.4B sales, Q1 FY27 FCF margin 33.5%). (3) EV/EBITDA, weight 0.2: (16 x ~$3.2B - ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt) / 0.575 = $82.4. The supervisor harmonized this leg to 16x from agents 1-4's 14-15.5x (agent 5 already used 16x), which double-counted the derating. Blend: 0.5 x 86.25 + 0.3 x 86 + 0.2 x 82.4 = $85.4, rounded to $85. Scenarios: bear $52 (20-22%), base $86-88 (53-55%), bull $118-125 (25%). Published 12-month distribution (2026-10-13): median (target) $78.92, mean $87.87 (+18.5%), 25th/75th percentile $56.46/$108.81. The ~2.45% dividend is on top. The research passed the citation gate on 2026-10-14 (clean: 78 checked, 11 fixed); no fix changed a number. TRIAL STANDARD MODEL, shown beside the published target and not the target: a standard model built on 2026-10-14 from the same research gives a model target of $85.40 at the research date's $78.69 spot (+8.5%; +15.2% against today's $74.16, derived 85.40 / 74.16), and research target (12m) $85.32 = 0.5 x $86.25 (P/E 18.75x on $4.60 NTM EPS) + 0.3 x $85.20 (5.0% FCF yield on $4.26/share) + 0.2 x $83.19 (16x EV/EBITDA). Bear/base/bull are $51.71/$85.32/$119.43 at 20/55/25%. Caveat: the 18.75x P/E sits at the top of, slightly above, the ~13.7-18.5x NTM P/E range of NXPI and ON (rebuilt by the citation gate from 2026-09-25 closes and StockAnalysis consensus EPS, time-weighted NTM), so the model leans on the high end of peer multiples. The published target remains $78.92.

catalysts.watch: Q4 guide vs seasonal, breadth of the industrial recovery, any sign of customers or distributors rebuilding inventory, pricing.

catalysts.watch: Auto guide, distribution inventory weeks, pricing commentary.

catalysts.why_it_moves: MCHP is a levered cyclical whose 18.5-19x multiple assumption is capped by a ~5.2% 10-yr yield (5.21% on 2026-10-13), and it carries ~$5.1B of net debt.
catalysts.watch: Statement and press conference; whether the 10-yr breaks above ~5.3%.

catalysts.event: MCHP Q2 FY27 results and December-quarter guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first print since the CFO guided GM flat into December, and it tests whether the Aug/Sep price increase replaces the September quarter's one-time licensing and repricing gains. The company has not announced the date: its IR calendar showed no upcoming events on 2026-10-14. The two prior Q2 calls were on 2024-11-05 and 2025-11-06.
catalysts.watch: Sales vs the $1.589-1.618B guide and EPS vs $0.91-0.95; GM holding 66-67%; the December guide vs seasonal; distributor inventory days (25 now); bookings and lead times; net-debt paydown; any buyback-timing change; first commentary on the VORAGO acquisition (2026-10-09, terms undisclosed, not expected to be material).

catalysts.why_it_moves: Management gives mid-quarter commentary on bookings and the channel.
catalysts.watch: Bookings tone, lead times, any change to the 'GM flat into December' message.

catalysts.why_it_moves: On 2025-12-02 MCHP raised its December-quarter guidance to the high end of the range. A repeat would confirm the cycle; silence is neutral.
catalysts.watch: Any press release or 8-K revising December-quarter sales or EPS guidance.

catalysts.watch: December-quarter sales vs guide; commentary on March-quarter backlog.

catalysts.event: FOMC decisions (meetings Jan 26-27; Mar 16-17 with projections)
MCHP Q3 FY27 results and March-quarter guide (prior Q3 calls: 2025-02-06, 2026-02-05)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first quarter with the one-time GM items fully out and the price increase fully in. The March guide shows whether the upcycle extends into CY2027.
catalysts.watch: GM at or above 65-66%, distributor inventory days, book-to-bill, net debt/EBITDA progress toward a buyback restart.

risks.risk: The upcycle peaks around mid-2027, near the horizon, as the market starts pricing FY29 (forecasters' bear case $52 at 20-22%).
risks.signpost: Book-to-bill below 1, distributor inventory rising from 25 days, shortening lead times, or a December/March guide below seasonal.

risks.risk: Gross margin slips as the September quarter's one-time licensing and repricing gains roll off and the price increase fades.
risks.signpost: A December-quarter GM guide below 66%, or management walking back 'flat into December'.

risks.risk: Rates and sector derating compress the multiple regardless of fundamentals.
risks.signpost: The 10-yr holding above ~5.3% (5.21% on 2026-10-13; 5.17% on 2026-09-25), and TXN/NXPI trading lower on their October prints.

risks.risk: Leverage and dilution: $5.09B net debt, no buybacks, and the mandatory convertible (converts 2028-03-15) delivers more shares below ~$62.48, up to ~29.1M shares below ~$51.00 (vs 23.8M above $62.48).
risks.signpost: Quarterly net-debt paydown staying near the June quarter's ~$170M instead of rising; the stock below ~$62.5.

trade.position: none: 0 sh, $0 (MCHP is on the book's exclusion list; allocation binding = 'excluded')
trade.entry: No entry. For reference only, if the exclusion were lifted: the supervisor's plan was medium conviction, max 5% of the book, in two tranches (half at once, half after the Q2 FY27 print, ~2026-11-05, estimated).
trade.exit_or_add: There is nothing to exit. A buy would need two things. First, the exclusion lifted: it is a book-construction decision from 2026-10-01 (MCHP moves too much with AVGO; model correlation 0.38 to AVGO and 0.39 to NVDA, both holdings; BKNG took the slot). Second, a gate-clean re-run after the Q2 FY27 print that keeps the target clearly above spot. The published thesis-break stop is $55 (~12x FY28 consensus: 55 / 4.58 = 12.0) and the take-profit is $108.81 (the 75th percentile).

what_changes_our_mind: Q2 FY27 (~2026-11-05, estimated): GM at 66-67% with a December guide at or above seasonal and distributor inventory near 25 days would strengthen the research case. GM below 66% or a guide implying a sequential decline would mean the cycle is rolling before mid-2027.

A December or January pre-announcement above guidance, as on 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-05, plus a buyback-restart signal would move us toward the $95 weighted analyst median. Distributor inventory rising materially from 25 days, or management citing destocking, would move us toward the $52 bear case.

For the book, the exclusion is the binding constraint. If MCHP's correlation to AVGO/NVDA falls, or AVGO leaves the book, a re-run with the target still above spot would make it buyable. A close below $55 ends the thesis.
